Recent studies suggest a possible association between dephosphorylated-uncarboxylated MGP (dp-ucMGP) and glomerular filtration rate (GFR). This study aimed to establish normative data in an adult Caucasian population and to explore the potential utility of dp-ucMGP in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) with and without diabetic kidney disease (DKD). Healthy volunteers (HVs) (cross-sectional study) and participants with DM (prospective cohort study) were recruited. Plasma dp-ucMGP was measured using the IDS®-iSYS Ina Ktif (dp-ucMGP) assay. Of the HVs recruited (n = 208), 67(32.2%) were excluded leaving a reference population of 141(67.8%) metabolically healthy participants with normal kidney function. Plasma dp-ucMGP RIs were <300–532 pmol/L. There were 100 eligible participants with DKD and 92 with DM without DKD. For the identification of participants with DKD, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for dp-ucMGP was 0.842 (95%CI:0.799–0.880; p < 0.001). Plasma dp-ucMGP demonstrated similar ability to urine albumin:creatinine ratio (uACR) to detect participants with DM and renal function decline. Among patients with DM, there was a negative correlation between natural log (LN) dp-ucMGP and eGFR (r = −0.7041; p < 0.001) and rate of change in renal function [%change (r = −0.4509; p < 0.001)] and a positive correlation between LN dp-ucMGP and LN uACR (r = 0.3392; p < 0.001). These results suggest the potential for plasma dp-ucMGP with well-defined RIs to identify adults at high risk for vascular disease in the context of progressive DKD. Subject terms Predictive markers Chronic kidney disease Biochemistry Predictive markers Diabetes complications https://doi.org/10.13039/100010661 EC | Horizon 2020 Framework Programme (EU Framework Programme for Research and Innovation H2020) 634086 Islam Md Nahidul issue-copyright-statement © The Author(s) 2019 Introduction Matrix Gla-protein (MGP), a 10-kDA secreted protein 1 , is a member of the family of vitamin K-dependent proteins (Gla [γ-carboxyglutamate] proteins) 2 . It is expressed by arterial medial vascular smooth muscle cells, fibroblasts, chondrocytes and endothelial cells 3 in a variety of tissues including the arterial wall, heart, lungs and kidneys 4 . MGP is a potent inhibitor of vascular calcification 5 . Mice that lack MGP develop to term but die within two months due to arterial calcification which leads to blood-vessel rupture 6 . Keutel syndrome, a rare autosomal recessive disorder, is caused by a loss-of-function mutation of MGP that results in abnormal calcification 7 . Increased vascular calcification leads to increased MGP transcription and production of dephosphorylated-uncarboxylated MGP (dp-ucMGP) 8 . Post-translational modification of dp-ucMGP is necessary for it to acquire its full calcification inhibitory activity: dp-ucMGP (inactive) undergoes γ-glutamate carboxylation to form dephosphorylated-carboxylated MGP (dp-cMGP) (intermediate) followed by serine phosphorylation to form active phosphorylated-carboxylated MGP (p-cMGP). Vitamin K hydroquinone is an essential cofactor for the enzyme γ-glutamylcarboxylase that catalyses the conversion of dp-ucMGP to dp-cMGP. Plasma concentration of dp-ucMGP is considered to be a better indicator of vascular vitamin K status than other components of the MGP system and correlates with vascular stiffness in the general population and in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) 3 , 9 , 10 . Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) have increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality 11 , 12 . Cardiovascular disease (CVD) affects approximately 30% of all persons with type 2 DM (T2DM); reducing life expectancy by up to 10 years 12 . DM is the leading cause of CKD worldwide (known as diabetic kidney disease (DKD)) 13 and in conjunction with kidney disease is highly associated with vascular calcification 14 . In the population-based NHANES III study in those with T2DM, the subgroup with evidence of CKD accounted for most or all of the excess cardiovascular mortality risk compared to those without DM 15 . Elevated plasma dp-ucMGP was associated with vascular calcification in patients with different degrees of kidney disease 10 , 16 and independently associated with lower renal function 9 . Plasma dp-ucMGP was also independently associated with peripheral vascular calcification 3 , carotid femoral pulse wave velocity 17 and aortic pulse wave velocity 18 . Aortic pulse wave velocity is an independent predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality 19 . Vitamin K supplementation (VKS) has been associated with a reduction in vascular calcification and plasma dp-ucMGP concentrations although further studies are needed 20 . Thus, measurement of plasma dp-ucMGP has the potential to be a marker of effective VKS. Finally, vitamin K-dependent proteins such as dp-ucMGP are associated with the combined endpoint of CVD or mortality 20 . There is a significant unmet clinical need for the identification of biomarkers that serve as predictors of renal function decline 21 and/or identification of patients at risk of CVD with differing degrees of renal impairment. To identify the utility of a biomarker in a disease process, it is important firstly to understand how this biomarker behaves in a healthy population with no underlying disease processes. To our knowledge, this is the first report to establish robust reference intervals (RIs) for dp-ucMGP measured using the IDS®-iSYS, an automated immunoassay analyzer based on chemiluminescent technology, in metabolically healthy adults with normal kidney function. Previous studies have established reference intervals for total MGP using a sandwich ELISA kit 22 and explored the relationships between dp-ucMGP concentrations measured using a sandwich dual-antibody ELISA and coronary artery calcification and vitamin K status in healthy women 23 , 24 . The primary aims of this study were to establish normative data for dp-ucMGP in an Irish Caucasian population and to explore the promise of dp-ucMGP as a new biomarker in patients with DKD. The secondary aim was to compare plasma dp-ucMGP and urine albumin:creatinine ratio (uACR) in the identification of individuals with rapid decline in renal function.

molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.activity_type_context: Vascular calcification, diabetic kidney disease (DKD), renal function decline, cardiovascular disease risk, and vitamin K status
molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: Matrix Gla-protein (MGP) is a potent inhibitor of vascular calcification. Inactive dephosphorylated-uncarboxylated MGP (dp-ucMGP) requires post-translational modification (γ-glutamate carboxylation and serine phosphorylation), with vitamin K as an essential cofactor for carboxylation, to become active phosphorylated-carboxylated MGP (p-cMGP). Increased vascular calcification leads to increased MGP transcription and production of dp-ucMGP. High plasma dp-ucMGP reflects vitamin K insufficiency, which is associated with increased vascular calcification, lower renal function, increased cardiovascular disease risk, and arterial stiffness. Renal function decline also leads to increased plasma dp-ucMGP levels, potentially due to reduced excretion and specific kidney pathophysiological effects (e.g., tubulointerstitial MGP associating with fibrosis/injury). Vitamin K therapy is proposed to reduce dp-ucMGP and potentially slow vascular calcification.

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: Reference intervals for plasma dp-ucMGP in metabolically healthy Caucasian adults with normal kidney function were <300–532 pmol/L. Plasma dp-ucMGP levels show a clear association with disease intensity and progression, exhibiting a significant, stepwise increase with disease severity (Healthy Volunteers < Diabetes Mellitus without DKD < Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD)) and progressively increasing across CKD stages (2/3 to 5). Elevated plasma dp-ucMGP is associated with vascular calcification in patients with varying kidney disease severity. Decliners of renal function (both absolute and percentage change in eGFR) consistently showed significantly higher plasma dp-ucMGP levels than non-decliners. There is a negative correlation between LN dp-ucMGP and eGFR, implying higher dp-ucMGP with declining renal function, where small absolute changes at lower eGFRs have a greater impact on dp-ucMGP. The association with renal function change was stronger when expressed as percentage change. Vitamin K2 supplementation resulted in reductions in dp-ucMGP, with 27% reduction over 6 weeks and 10.7% over 270 days.
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: Plasma dp-ucMGP effectively distinguishes Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD) from Diabetes Mellitus without DKD and healthy volunteers, with an AUC of 0.842 (sensitivity 67.0%, specificity 91%) at an optimum cut-off >557 pmol/L for the combined group, and AUC 0.747 (sensitivity 64.7%, specificity 80%) at a cut-off >570 pmol/L for DKD vs. DM without DKD. It demonstrated a similar ability to urine albumin:creatinine ratio (uACR) in detecting DM patients with renal function decline, though uACR was stronger at a specific eGFR decline threshold (≤−4.5 mL/min/1.73 m2). Plasma dp-ucMGP shows moderate ability to distinguish decliners from non-decliners (AUC 0.696 for absolute eGFR decline and 0.800 for % eGFR decline). It is independently associated with peripheral vascular calcification, carotid femoral pulse wave velocity, and aortic pulse wave velocity, indicating its specificity for vascular health markers. Unlike medical conditions, age per se does not significantly influence dp-ucMGP, and there was no significant difference between smokers and non-smokers.

clinical_implication_and_population.target_population: Metabolically healthy adult Caucasian population with normal kidney function (for reference intervals), participants with Diabetes Mellitus (DM) with and without Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD), including those with Type 2 DM (T2DM), particularly those with peripheral artery disease and heart failure. This also includes renal function decliners, patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) at various stages, community-dwelling older adults (>55 years), and haemodialysis patients. The biomarker also targets adults at high risk for vascular disease in the context of progressive DKD.
clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: Plasma dp-ucMGP has potential diagnostic and prognostic utility for identifying and diagnosing Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD) and for predicting progressive renal function decline in patients with DM. It can identify adults at high risk for vascular disease within the context of progressive DKD. High plasma dp-ucMGP is associated with increased vascular stiffness, peripheral vascular calcification, carotid femoral pulse wave velocity, aortic pulse wave velocity, and an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) or mortality. Therefore, dp-ucMGP has potential to predict long-term vascular health, and interventions like vitamin K therapy targeting high dp-ucMGP may offer clinical benefits by slowing vascular calcification.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: Plasma dp-ucMGP serves as a diagnostic utility for Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD) and renal function decline. It is also a predictive and prognostic marker for renal decline and cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, enabling risk stratification for individuals at high risk for vascular disease. High dp-ucMGP indicates adverse risk, while interventions like vitamin K therapy to reduce dp-ucMGP may offer potential protective benefits against vascular calcification.

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment:
Robust reference intervals (RIs) for plasma dp-ucMGP were established using the IDS®-iSYS automated immunoassay analyzer in metabolically healthy Caucasian adults with normal kidney function, enhancing reliability. The assay demonstrated good analytical performance, including verified linearity (1:6 dilution, 100  
  ± 10% recovery), good intra-assay (4.02-2.85%) and inter-assay (5.57-3.22%) precision, and stability at -80 °C for 9 months and across freeze-thaw cycles. Bias was 6.1-9.0%. Hemolysis effects on recovery were observed. Plasma dp-ucMGP is considered a better indicator of vascular vitamin K status and shows independent associations with various vascular health markers. It effectively distinguishes healthy individuals and DM patients without DKD from those with DKD, though accuracy decreased when healthy volunteers were excluded. A limitation is that 39.0% of healthy volunteers had concentrations below the assay's lower limit of quantification (300 pmol/L). The accuracy is affected by 'imperfect gold standard bias' (eGFR/uACR vs. renal biopsy), and RIs' generalisability is limited to Northern European Caucasians. The absence of a validation cohort is also a noted limitation.
recommended_alternatives: More sensitive assays are necessary for reporting values < 300 pmol/L.
Further studies are required to determine and definitively confirm whether gender-specific reference intervals are necessary.
For identifying renal function decliners, using percentage change rather than absolute change in renal function may be more sensitive, requiring further study.
GFR should ideally be measured using a reference method instead of the CKD-EPI equation for greater accuracy.
Renal biopsy is considered the true 'gold standard' for DKD diagnosis (though not always practical).
Urinary Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (uACR) is a comparative biomarker for distinguishing renal function decliners.
